messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: Datadog EU ingestion backlog detected (logs + partial metrics). Paging SRE. :rotating_light:

nina: seeing log gaps for eu-west-2 services in the Observability console. span->log joins failing for ~30-45m.

josh: traces arriving but the log sidecar reports backpressure errors: \"upstream write slow\". error detectors that rely on log patterns aren't firing.

riley: support ticket influx: a few customers report missing error emails. told them were investigating; no customer-visible downtime.

ops-bot: datadog-bot: \"We are aware of increased ingestion latency for EU ingestion endpoints. Teams impacted: logs/metrics. We are working on backlog processing.\" https://status.datadoghq.com

maria: mitigation plan idea: 1) enable local disk buffering and S3 flush on shippers so nothing is lost, 2) enable CloudWatch-only forwards for ERROR/CRITICAL, 3) lower debug-level sampling to 5%.

nina: implemented disk buffering and immediate S3 flush for the following namespaces: api-prod, web-frontend, workers. Verified sample files on s3://redwood-observability/backups/eu/

josh: applying sampling reduction across worker pools now. command: ```kubectl -n prod set env deploy/worker LOG_SAMPLING=0.05 && kubectl rollout restart deploy/worker```

riley: standing up a tiny Lambda forwarder to push ERROR lines to CloudWatch / Alertmanager so PD alerts keep firing.

support-bot: posted canned customer message to #support-runbook: \"Were experiencing delayed log/metric ingestion in EU; app health unaffected; weve enabled backups and alternate alerting. Will update when ingestion normalizes.\"

ops-bot: PagerDuty: new incident PD-OBS-2146 created.

datadog-bot: \"We are continuing to process a backlog caused by an upstream storage replication issue. No ETA yet. Updates to follow.\"

maria: I opened a ticket with Datadog (DD-110200) and asked for an ETA + best practice for replays. They asked us to avoid bulk replays until backlog drained.

josh: important: do not run any replays or bulk log uploads into Datadog while DD is draining. That can cause duplicate spikes and more lag. Adding note to runbook.

nina: temporary alerting changes: metric-only alerts for service error counts and latency have been created; log-detector alerts are muted for affected services. Dashboard \"OBS-EU-Fallback\" created with S3 arrival times and CW error counts.

riley: customer impact summary for handoff: some alert noise missing (log-based detectors), customers may see delayed error emails; application functioning normally. backup logs landing in S3 for audit.

oncall-next: taking handoff at +20. please list outstanding actions.

maria: outstanding: 1) monitor DD ticket DD-110200 and datadog status page, 2) ensure S3 files continue to arrive and aren't throttled (check arrival_time vs created_time), 3) keep error-forwarder to CloudWatch active, 4) do not replay logs to Datadog until explicit OK from DD.

josh: added monitoring alerts for S3 lateness (if a file isn't visible in 10m after creation) and disk buffer pressure on shippers.

riley: made a note for support: if customers request logs, provide S3 path and a short explanation. enterprise AE asked for hourly updates; assigned to account team.

ops-bot: NOTE: If Datadog confirms backlog cleared, plan for cautious ramp: sampling 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% over 15m steps, disable CloudWatch forwarder, keep S3 backup for 6h before purging. Document rollback steps.

oncall-next: got it. taking over. Ill post a 15:30 UTC status update and keep the channel updated.

ops-bot: Incident state: mitigation in progress. Please avoid configuration churn (no mass changes) unless needed for mitigation.

support-bot: final note for this phase: no customer outages reported. will escalate if error alerts continue missing after an hour.

maria: leaving handoff note: runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/datadog-eu-ingest-backlog. keep this thread as the source of truth for state changes.

oncall-next: acknowledged, thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
